Nyircsaholy Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírcsaholy, Hungary

Not demolished. Following the construction of a railway line through Nyírcsaholy in 1904, the village became a local commercial hub and its Jewish population grew; an official community was organized in 1832 and a synagogue built in 1849. In 1941, 32 Jewish men taken for forced labor perished in Ukraine or at the Mauthausen and Günskirchen concentration camps; in May 1944, the remaining Jews were deported to Auschwitz after being held in the Mátészalka Ghetto since late April. This Jewish section, established as early as 1855, per its oldest tombstone, sits within the village's municipal cemetery.
